# Handoff checklist — `[CLIENT]` / `[PROJECT]`

**Date:** `[ ]` · **SOW:** `[ ]`

> The handoff is what makes the client stay because they want to, not because
> they're stuck. It is also the single easiest place to look more professional
> than the competition, because most of this simply doesn't happen elsewhere.

---

## Code and infrastructure

- [ ] Repository transferred or client granted owner access
- [ ] Client owns the hosting account and the deployment
- [ ] Domain and DNS under the client's control
- [ ] All third-party accounts in the client's name, billed to the client
- [ ] Environment variables documented (names and purpose — **never values in
      the doc**)
- [ ] Deployment process documented and reproducible

## Documentation

- [ ] How the system works — architecture in plain language
- [ ] How to make common changes
- [ ] How to deploy
- [ ] Known limitations and deliberate trade-offs
- [ ] **SBOM and licence scan report**
- [ ] Where the data lives and how backups work

## Walkthrough

- [ ] Live walkthrough delivered
- [ ] **Recorded** (~30 min screen recording) and handed over — reusable, and
      saves you giving the same session three times
- [ ] Client's own users trained, if more than the main contact

## Credentials and access

- [ ] All credentials transferred securely — **never over plain email**
- [ ] Client has confirmed receipt and can log in unaided
- [ ] **Your access removed or reduced to what the support window needs**
- [ ] Removal confirmed to the client in writing

*Holding access you no longer need is an avoidable liability. If the client's
system is breached later, you don't want to be a live credential holder.*

## Commercial

- [ ] Final invoice issued and paid — **IP transfers on full payment**
      ([MSA §4.1](../contracts/msa-template.md))
- [ ] Written acceptance received
- [ ] Support window start and end dates confirmed in writing
- [ ] Client told exactly what is and isn't covered during support

## Case study groundwork

- [ ] **Baseline numbers from kickoff retrieved** — ready to re-measure at retro
- [ ] Testimonial requested *(now — at delivery, when they're happiest)*
- [ ] Google review requested — the main trust asset for a faceless brand
- [ ] Written permission to publish results confirmed
      ([MSA §4.6](../contracts/msa-template.md))
- [ ] Retro scheduled for two weeks out
